Reopened editor must show split type exact, their switch off, my box 100.00, AND their box still showing the typed 40 (not blank); re-include, restore 60/40, save again and confirm the redirect
Regression sweep of the v1 proofs that touch this file: T-2 keyboard/arrow split control, T-5 short-split refusal sentence rendered once, T-6 double-submit single write
risks: The PR branch's editor markup differs from main's (restyle with switch/disabled); the fix description is behavioral (no disabled on split.N.value, readOnly instead) so it applies regardless of the exact class strings
readOnly inputs stay keyboard-focusable where disabled ones did not: one extra Tab stop per excluded row, announced with its label; accepted as the honest cost of keeping the value submittable

work_order.root_cause: PR #43's restyled split row renders the excluded participant's value input with the disabled attribute. A disabled control contributes nothing to the submission, so split.N.value for the excluded row arrived missing; readExpenseForm yields '' for it and parseSplitValue returns null, which is stored as inputValue null. On reopen getExpenseEditorData renders splitValueText('exact', null) = '', the blank box QA saw in T-4. The server contract was never broken — validation.ts promises a left-out row keeps whatever was typed and validation.test.ts proves an excluded row submitted WITH a value keeps it — it was starved of the value at submit. The exclusion itself persisted correctly (an unchecked checkbox submits nothing, which the schema reads as included=false).

cases: Exact-split T-4 replay at the boundary: FormData with split.0 included/100 plus split.1 excluded carrying value 40 parses ok and the draft keeps the excluded line as {included:false, value:4000} with splitValueText rendering 40.00, not blank

The disabled-input shape of the same form (split.1.value field omitted, which is what the browser submits for a disabled control) yields inputValue null and a blank read-back, documenting the trap the client must not fall into
Equal-split expenses still carry no per-member value fields and parse exactly as before
Render ExpenseEditor with an exact split where one participant is excluded with a typed value: their split.N.value input renders that value and carries NO disabled attribute (readOnly instead)
Included rows render normally editable inputs with no readOnly and no disabled
The include checkbox remains the sole emitter of split.N.included in the rendered markup

work_order.understanding: The v1 plan was wrong on exactly the point that failed: it specified a styled include switch for leaving members out but never constrained what exclusion does to the row's value input, treating the switch as pure presentation. The implementer chose disabled for the excluded input; a disabled input submits nothing, so the excluded member's typed 40 arrived as '' and was stored as inputValue null, reopening blank — while the plan's own evidence quoted the server comment promising the typed value is kept, without pinning the client behavior that delivers it. The exclusion itself worked (unchecked checkbox submits nothing, read as included=false). Second defect in v1: it placed the new Dialog/Menu contract test at components/dialog-contract.test.ts, which vitest never collects (include is lib/app/scripts only), so part of its proof would run nowhere. BUG-2 (activity-excerpt overflow) is pre-existing — activity-feed.tsx is byte-identical between main and the PR — and stays out of scope.

issue_snapshot.title: Expense editor and settle-up sheet with confirms and menus
issue_snapshot.body:
Recording an expense correctly the first time and settling a suggested transfer take seconds, with the amount prominent and destructive choices confirmed.

UI face: payer records an expense amount-first with live per-member shares and a sticky save, and settles up through a prefilled sheet instead of inline row forms, with confirms on destructive choices. Contract face: consumes money inputs, segmented control, dialogs/sheets, toasts, and notice-param success treatment from piece 1; submits through the existing expense and payment Server Actions with identical payloads and validation, defining no new endpoint. Follows docs/ui.md Expense editor and Settle-up flow structures and states exactly.

**Risk.** Touches the two money-writing surfaces (expense amounts with live shares, settle-up prefilled amounts); money math and payloads are unchanged and review must reject any logic change.

**Out of scope**
- Any split-math, remainder-rule, balance, simplification, or transaction change
- Group page sections, members, activity, and profile screens (sibling pieces)
- Dark mode

Covers: TR-11, S-8
Part of #31.
Depends on #33.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** EXPENSE EDITOR: amount is first, large, autofocused money input with group currency prefix and decimal input mode, followed by description, styled date picker with human reading, and category plus note.
- **IAC-2** EXPENSE EDITOR: payer area defaults to me with a single payer; Paid by several people progressively reveals per-person parts; split-type segmented control (equal, exact, percentage, shares) shows only that type's per-member rows with avatar, name, and live computed share.
- **IAC-3** EXPENSE EDITOR: live sum and remainder line confirms parts equal the total; validation on blur and submit names the shortfall and its size; reopening shows the stored split type and each member input exactly as entered.
- **IAC-4** EXPENSE EDITOR: sticky bottom bar holds primary Save and Cancel with back-to-group; saving disables Save with Saving plus spinner, never unmounts mid-save, double submit is impossible, and failed save keeps all input with retry.
- **IAC-5** SETTLE-UP: per-transfer Settle up opens a centred dialog on desktop and bottom sheet on phones with the who-pays-whom line, suggested amount prefilled and editable for partial payment, optional date, one Record payment confirm plus cancel; no inline amount forms on rows.
- **IAC-6** SETTLE-UP: confirming records the payment and updates feed plus balances with a toast or redirect notice; after a partial payment the confirmation shows what remains owed; failed record keeps the sheet open with all input, names the problem, and offers retry.
- **IAC-7** Deleting a recorded expense or payment confirms in a dialog naming the object and its consequence; destructive pending and focus-trap plus focus-return hold; every control is keyboard reachable with visible focus at 375px and 1280px.

review.title: Expense-row relative dates ('Today'/'Yesterday'/'Tomorrow') are computed from the server's UTC clock, so they can be off by one for viewers away from UTC.
review.detail:
Expense-row relative dates ('Today'/'Yesterday'/'Tomorrow') are computed from the server's UTC clock, so they can be off by one for viewers away from UTC.

`app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:236`

Evidence: app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:236 `const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (UTC) feeds humanDateLabel at :555. toISOString is UTC: a viewer at UTC-8 reading the group page at 6pm local sees server-tomorrow, so today's expenses read 'Yesterday'. The editor avoids this by reading the clock client-side post-mount; the server-rendered rows cannot, and the relative word replaces (not accompanies) the absolute date.

Fix: Render the absolute day-month next to the relative word on server rows (so the row is never wrong, only less chatty), or move the relative label into a tiny client island that reads the viewer's day.

review.title: The restyled per-member include switch shrank its touch target below the ui.md 44px minimum: the label carries no min-height and the visible track is h-6 (24px tall), where the control it replaces sat in a min-h-11 (44px) label.
review.detail:
The restyled per-member include switch shrank its touch target below the ui.md 44px minimum: the label carries no min-height and the visible track is h-6 (24px tall), where the control it replaces sat in a min-h-11 (44px) label.

`components/expense-editor.tsx:131`

Evidence: PR branch components/expense-editor.tsx:131 renders <label class="relative inline-flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center"> around an sr-only checkbox and an h-6 w-11 track, so the hit area is 24px tall; the replaced markup used <label class="flex min-h-11 items-center gap-2">. ui.md Density requires touch targets of at least 44px.

Fix: Give the IncludeSwitch label a 44px hit area (e.g. min-h-11 min-w-11 justify-center, or padding around the track) while keeping the checkbox-underneath payload exactly as is.

review.title: Refused payment submissions now invalidate the home and activity caches although nothing changed: revalidateBalances(outcome.groupId) runs for every outcome with groupId undefined on refusals, and the undefined branch still calls revalidatePath('/') and revalidatePath('/activity'). Before, refusals returned early without revalidating anything.
review.detail:
Refused payment submissions now invalidate the home and activity caches although nothing changed: revalidateBalances(outcome.groupId) runs for every outcome with groupId undefined on refusals, and the undefined branch still calls revalidatePath('/') and revalidatePath('/activity'). Before, refusals returned early without revalidating anything.

`lib/settle/actions.ts:215`

Evidence: PR branch lib/settle/actions.ts:123-130 makes groupId optional and always revalidates '/' and '/activity'; calls at :215 and :279 run unconditionally after withDb. Old code called revalidateBalances(access.group.id) only on the two success paths. Full suite passes either way (466 tests), so this is cache churn, not wrong data.

Fix: Only revalidate when something changed, e.g. gate the call on outcome.groupId being set, restoring the previous refusal behavior exactly.

The refusal text, description, amount and per-member split values all persist; only the included choices are discarded. Open /groups/:id/expenses/new, fill amount 500 and any description.
Turn B's Include switch off (B reads excluded, A stays included).
Fill amount with not-a-number (or otherwise trigger a refused save) and press Add expense.

qa.suspected_cause: The editor's state writers (changeParticipant and the field setters in _pr/components/expense-editor.tsx) preserve values across the useActionState refusal resync, but nothing re-applies the included flags after the action state resets them; the controlled checked={participant.included} binding plus the identical action wiring exist unchanged on the base commit, so this reads as a pre-existing state-resync defect, not a regression from this PR's IncludeSwitch restyle. A direct behavioral check on the base commit was attempted but the base preview wedges under Playwright traffic (health timeouts, aborted requests), so the call rests on the identical code architecture, not on a green base run.
